text:
jamie: Quick oncall swap — I'm handing primary to @morgan for the 10:00-18:00 UTC window. Few quick notes before I sign off:

jamie: Current state: no active P1s. Yesterday's DB latency incident is closed (postmortem posted). No ongoing customer escalations.

jamie: Primary responsibilities for @morgan:
- keep an eye on 95p/99p generation latency on prod (dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/latency)
- page infra-oncall if DB error-rate > 2% sustained for 5m or if replication lag > 30s
- page runtime-oncall for model-serving regressions (95p > 3s or error spike)
- for suspected data-exfil or auth failures immediately page sec@redwood and @sam-security

morgan: ack — taking it. I have the runbooks open, will monitor the dashboards.

jamie: Runbook pointers (shortcuts):
- main oncall play: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-main
- paging matrix: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging-matrix
- incident triage checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-triage

jamie: Escalation rules (TL;DR):
```
# P1 (customer-facing outage, data-loss, or >80% traffic degraded):
1) Page infra-pager (+ call) immediately
2) If no ack in 5m -> page eng-platform lead @devon (pager: +1-555-0102)
3) If still unresolved after 15m -> page oncall-manager @alex and CSM @priya (conference bridge)
4) For security-sensitive -> also page security lead @sam-security and sec@redwood
```

jamie: Minor alerts (latency spikes, increased 5xx): triage in thread. Only escalate to call when impact persists > 10m or SLO breach > 30m. Use reactions for quick ack :eyes: :thumbsup:.

devon: Adding a note on escalation matrix — for Dedicated customers with SLA, escalate to sales-eng on the first 10m if it looks like capacity/queueing. Contact list is on the paging matrix link.

priya: CSMs — if you see a customer-facing incident that might need a proactive outreach, ping me in #customer-success and I'll open a support case; for P1s I join the bridge.

morgan: quick question — weekend overnight coverage gap check: we still have no designated secondary between 02:00-04:00 UTC Sat/Sun, right?

jamie: yes that's correct. Ops rota hasn't filled that block. If you get an alert in that window, follow the 'bridge fallback' section in the oncall-main runbook: page infra-team, then fallback to oncall-manager.

devon: For paging mechanics — please use the pager for P1s (phone call) and the Slack page for P2/P3. Example page tags: @pager/infra, @pager/runtime, @pager/security. If pager returns no ack, send SMS and then escalate to the phone list in the paging matrix.

morgan: ACK. I'll set a quick personal watch for the DB dashboards for the first 30m to make sure no latent issues.

jamie: small checklist before handoff (do these out loud in thread):
- confirm no active incidents -> done
- confirm alerts muted for low-prio test jobs -> done
- post handoff in #eng-oncall w/ contact numbers -> doing now

incident-bot: [AUTOGEN] 1802000120 - New alert: prod/runtime/95p-latency spike (source: autoscale-probe). Severity: P2.

morgan: saw the bot — looking. spinning up quick investigation: checking recent deploys and model-variant routing.

morgan: preliminary: spike tied to a burst of long-context requests from one client, 95p peaked at 3.2s for ~4m. Not seeing increased 5xx.

devon: if it's single-client burst, consider short-term routing to smaller-context model or temporary rate-limit on that API key. That's in the optimize runbook.

morgan: will apply rate-limit with the traffic-control tool (command):
```bash
trafficctl limit --api-key abcd-1234 --qps 0.5 --ttl 15m
```
morgan: applied. monitoring.

morgan: spike subsided, 95p back to 1.1s. No escalation required. Leaving a note in the incident tracker.

jamie: perfect — thanks. That covers the swap. I'll be offline after 10:05 UTC. @morgan you have primary, @devon you're backup for major escalations, @alex is the exec contact for P1s.

morgan: got it. thanks jamie :rocket:
